g.text: Pencil writes · finger scrolls · space grows as you write
Thm. V f.d. over F, α ∈ End(V), χ_α(t) = det(tι − α)
Pf (F = ℂ). Pick a basis v₁, …, vₙ with [α] upper △,
diagonal λ₁, …, λₙ. Put Uᵢ = ⟨v₁, …, vᵢ⟩, U₀ = 0.
General F: pass to a splitting field?
Another screen of space appears when you write near the bottom
Since dim End(V) = n², the maps ι, α, …, αn² are linearly dependent,
so some polynomial kills α. Cayley–Hamilton names one of degree n.
Let V be an n-dimensional vector space over a field F, and α ∈ End(V).
choose a basis v1 , …, vn in which α is upper triangular with
diagonal λ1 , …, λn (possible because χα splits over ℂ), and put
αvi = λi vi + (terms in v1 , …, vi−1 ),
so (α − λi ι)Ui ⊆ Ui−1 . Applying the factors for i = n, …, 1
in turn drops one level each time:
χα (α) V = (α − λ1 ι) ⋯ (α − λn ι) V ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ U0 = 0. ∎
run the same argument over a field extension in which χα splits;
χα (α) = 0 is a statement about entries in F, so it holds over F.
each factor (α − λi ι) peels one layer off the flag U1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ Un .
